A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TPS-DPS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial revision and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original molecular simulations and synthetic experiments in Table 1, along with trajectory visualizations and component ablations in Figure 9.

after.justification: v5 reports original simulation results in Tables 1–2, component ablations in Figure 6, computational measurements in Appendix C, and additional comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The log-variance objective, learned control variate, replay buffer, simulated annealing, scale-based bias force, and relaxed indicator are retained. Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix into the main text. Expanded explanations and the new proof do not establish a changed sampling procedure.

E1.justification: v5 retains double-well, Alanine Dipeptide, and Chignolin experiments, removes Polyproline Helix isomerization, and adds folding experiments for Trp-cage, BBA, and BBL with 20, 28, and 47 residues. This substantially extends protein coverage while removing a distinct isomerization task.

E2.justification: UMD, SMD, and PIPS remain the main baseline families. Appendix E expands the existing force-based KL ablation with a reverse-KL potential variant. Two-way shooting is mentioned in Section 4.2, but no corresponding table, figure, or experimental protocol establishes its participation.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes Chignolin training from 1000 to 100 rollouts. Appendix B.4 changes TICA trajectory recording from 1 ps to 2 ps and specifies 2 fs integration. v5 replaces the Chignolin SMD(15k) comparison with SMD(20k), introduces 400 K protocols for the added proteins, and adds computational-cost metrics. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds an equivariance ablation in Figure 6, a potential-based reverse-KL control and trajectory comparison in Appendix E, and computational-cost analysis in Appendix C. The original five component ablations remain, but v4's SMD force-constant sensitivity and THP–ETS trade-off study in Figure 8 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report RMSD and ETS with accompanying plus/minus values and average ablation learning curves over eight seeds. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: The double-well and Alanine benchmark values and most Chignolin entries are retained. New TPS-DPS(S) hit rates are 81.25%, 84.38%, and 43.75% for Trp-cage, BBA, and BBL, alongside new ablation and computational-cost results. Polyproline results and the SMD sensitivity results disappear. The replacement Chignolin SMD scores use a different force constant and cannot establish a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A.3 add Proposition 1 and its proof of strict distance reduction after a sufficiently small bias-only position update and realignment, assuming nonzero initial distance. This extends v4's positive-inner-product observation. Appendix C also adds asymptotic cost arguments; the existing log-variance and discrete-loss derivations remain.

C1.justification: The central CV-free sampling and accuracy/diversity claims remain. However, the introduction strengthens the scale-based force claim from locally decreasing distance to decreasing it 'for every MD step.' That wording exceeds the new proposition's conditional guarantee for sufficiently small bias-only updates.

C2.justification: v5 specifies the tested protein-size boundary, identifies proteins above 500 residues as unexplored, and adds untested PLUMED/DMFF integration limitations. The cross-system generalization limitation remains. Section 4.3 also overgeneralizes failure of the force and potential variants: Table 2 reports a 12.50% Trp-cage hit rate for TPS-DPS(P).

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies configurations for the added proteins and revises Chignolin and TICA details. Appendix C newly identifies the RTX A5000 GPU and specifies timing conventions and simulated-path counts. The disclosed network architectures, learning rates, gradient clipping, and code/project links are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of Sipka et al. (2023) and Schreiner et al. (2024), elaborates Du et al. (2024), and discusses mixing and rejection limitations of shooting methods. Background and implementation references also change. These refine the context while preserving the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations undergo substantial rewriting. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, the experimental narrative is reorganized around fast-folding proteins, and the appendices gain separate proof, cost, visualization, and reverse-KL comparison sections.

P2.justification: v5 splits and expands the benchmark table, merges the double-well and Alanine trajectory figures, adds a bias-force-field illustration and comparison tables, and reorganizes case-study panels. The Chignolin trajectory display becomes a four-protein appendix grid. The SMD sensitivity plot and standalone Alanine/Polyproline snapshot figure are removed.

improvement.justification: The added 20–47-residue protein experiments and computational measurements materially strengthen scalability and efficiency claims that v4 supported with only one 10-residue protein-folding benchmark and limited cost evidence. The conditional descent proof and additional controls strengthen justification of the method. These gains outweigh the loss of Polyproline coverage and SMD sensitivity analysis, although the unconditional MD-step wording and blanket failure interpretation should be narrowed.
